summary: Roaming between guest & corp VLANs breaks SCEP certificate enrollment -> VPN/SSO onboarding failures at SF office
description: Issue summary: Multiple employees report that corporate VPN (WireGuard SSO onboarding) fails during initial device provisioning when devices roam between the guest SSID (office-guest) and the corporate SSID (redwood-corp) while the captive portal is active. Impact: ~12 users unable to finish device enrollment and obtain machine/user certs between 08:30 and 11:45 PDT on 2026-03-12; blocks VPN SSO onboarding and access to internal services. Initial triage indicates SCEP enrollment requests are timing out or returning incomplete cert chains. Suspected root cause: HTTP AIA/OCSP retrieval from CA is being blocked by an inline ACL on perimeter firewall when traffic hits the captive-portal redirect path, causing the client to fail to build the certificate chain and abort the EAP/SCEP flow. This appears to be triggered by SSID roam events that change VLAN and transiently route enrollment traffic through the guest-path enforcement chain.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Connect device to redwood-corp SSID, start onboarding (MDM enrollment triggers SCEP).
2) While enrollment is in progress, roam the device to office-guest SSID or force a VLAN switch via AP controller.
3) Observe SCEP request (ACME/SCEP POST) leaving device, then captive-portal HTTP redirect intercept occurs.
4) Client reports 'certificate chain incomplete' or times out after 30s and onboarding fails.
5) Repeat on macOS and Windows 11 — issue reproducible on both client types.
logs:
Sample logs:
- AP controller syslog: Mar 12 08:34:21 AP-02 roam: client 44:55:66:77:88:99 moved from VLAN 201 -> 120 (redwood-corp -> office-guest)
- Firewall (PA) traffic log: Mar 12 08:34:22 rule 'guest-web-redirect' allow http 10.8.34.112:80 -> 192.0.2.10:80; rule 'deny-http-to-external-ca' blocked 10.8.34.112:80 -> 198.51.100.5:80 (AIA)
- Client (macOS) Console: SCEP: 'Server responded but returned no CA cert chain'
- WireGuard onboarding: 'client enrollment failed: certificate verification error (chain incomplete)'
investigation_notes:
2026-03-12 09:00 - Initial report from ENG desk: several reports from hot desk area near AP-02.
2026-03-12 09:15 - Confirmed pattern: failures clustered around roaming/vlan change windows; when devices enroll staying persistently on redwood-corp SSID enrollment succeeds.
2026-03-12 09:40 - Packet capture on AP-02 uplink (pcap saved to /var/logs/pcaps/INT-714332-ap02.pcap): SCEP POST goes to CA but subsequent GET for AIA URL is rewritten to captive portal and never reaches CA.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Firewall rules audit: found legacy rule 'deny-http-to-external-ca' added 2025-11-01 to prevent outbound HTTP to known third-party CA host list; rule evaluated before captive-portal exception.
2026-03-12 10:30 - Tested adding temporary allow rule for 198.51.100.5 (CA AIA host) -> enrollment succeeded for repro device.
Hypothesis: captive-portal HTTP redirect + ordering of firewall ACLs causes AIA/OCSP fetches to be blocked during transient VLAN path; client cannot fetch intermediate CA or perform OCSP stapling checks, so SCEP fails.
Next steps: 1) Apply temporary targeted firewall exception for CA AIA/OCSP hosts for internal DHCP pool during onboarding windows. 2) Update AP controller to mark SCEP enrollment destinations as exempt from captive-portal redirects when EAP/SCEP flow is detected. 3) Run broader test across SF office APs and schedule a config change window.
workaround: Applied temporary firewall rule (PA rule id fw-temp-714332) to allow TCP/80 and TCP/443 to CA AIA and OCSP hosts (198.51.100.5, 203.0.113.44) from internal DHCP ranges for the duration of onboarding. Instructed on-site team to avoid roaming during enrollment as temporary mitigation. Pushed MDM policy to retry enrollments automatically once device returns to corp VLAN.
resolution: Mitigation implemented on 2026-03-12: temporary FW exception allowed SCEP/AIA traffic; immediate onboarding failures stopped. Planned permanent fix: reorder firewall ACLs to evaluate captive-portal redirect after exceptions for cert-enrollment endpoints, and create explicit AP controller bypass for SCEP/MDM enrollment flows. Change request CR-2026-0315 filed and scheduled for 2026-03-16 02:00-03:00 UTC maintenance window. Follow-up actions: update runbook with this failure mode, add monitoring alerts for certificate enrollment failure spikes, and whitelist known CA AIA/OCSP hosts in infra config repo PR referenced below.
